Findings: (a) line 43 (status/2032089795766129021): full tweet is a numbered 1-6 list ending '...6. AIs can drive hiqh quality development if properly constrained by strong engineers.' -- body blockquote stops after item 5 ('Architectural discipline is critical.') with no ellipsis, silently dropping item 6, even though the maintainer block's own gloss on line 103 explicitly says 'six fundamentals (... constrain AIs)', proving the omission was known and left undisclosed in body. (b) line 69 (status/2049124461127864613): full tweet continues two more paragraphs past the quoted text -- 'If we must review the code in detail then there is hardly any reason to use an AI. Humans are the weak link when it comes to code and syntax. But we are the strong link when it comes to conceptualization and mental models... A good suite of code quality and testing tools helps alot.' -- dropped without ellipsis; this content is directly on-thesis (testing tools) and its absence is a missed-not-misleading gap. (c) line 83 (status/2049453605237715058, already flagged in the prior technical pass for the Dykstra->Dijkstra spelling normalization): full tweet also continues past the quoted text with 'The formalism can be in the way acceptance, tests are written and executed, and in the tool suite that surrounds the activity of the AI.' -- this is arguably the single most on-thesis sentence in the entire source set (ties formalism directly to tests/tooling, the article's core claim) and it is the part left out, undisclosed, while the maintainer block claims 'All seven Uncle Bob blockquotes verified verbatim'. The other 4 quotes (status/2016166910698696916, /2032072361436983517, /2046222100164153548, /2049225231273767154) were independently confirmed complete via full-text mirror extraction -- true byte-for-byte matches (module @-mentions dropped from the reply-tweet at /2049225231273767154 is normal/non-deceptive editorial practice, not flagged).

The maintainer block's 'verified verbatim... oEmbed-verified' claim should be softened to 'verified against source' or the stamps re-run against full-text (not oEmbed-preview) content, since oEmbed's own truncation is what let this drift through two prior verification passes (2026-05-03 audit, 2026-05-25 freshness stamps).
